note: The constants whose DECLARATION LINE carries the fork's own `//@@MP` marker. Committed rather than read from `_refs/`, which is gitignored: a test that opened GameSounds.cs passed locally and failed in CI, which is the worst arrangement available. Regenerate with `grep -n '@@MP' 'Rogue Survivor Still Alive/Gameplay/GameSounds.cs'` and keep only the lines that also declare a constant.
why-declaration-line-only: The fork is inconsistent about where it puts the marker. Some constants carry it as a trailing comment on the declaration (`UNDEAD_EAT_PLAYER`, line 15); most carry it on a standalone comment line ABOVE the declaration (line 22 and twenty others). This fixture records the trailing form only, because that is the form that marks a single declaration unambiguously - a standalone marker above a declaration belongs to whatever follows it, which is a question about the next line rather than about this one. A constant with no trailing marker may still be fork-only by the other form; that is a different question and `tests/extended-audio.test.ts` is where the port's gating is actually decided.

unmarkedButAsserted.declaration: public const string MELEE_ATTACK_MISS_PLAYER = "player misses melee attack";
unmarkedButAsserted.why: Only its CALL SITE is marked (`//@@MP (Release 2)` where RogueGame.cs wires it up), which is the fork playing a sound the original game already shipped. So the sound belongs to both rulesets, and `extended-audio.test.ts` lists it in VANILLA_IDS rather than demanding an ExtendedAudio gate. Read the declaration, not the call site: reading the wrong one is how this constant was misfiled in the first place.
